A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 30-page paper, including Appendices A–K. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish complete, comparable material; differences are confined to the version stamp and a funding acknowledgment.

before.justification: v2 reports original bias-detection experiments, labeling-strategy simulations, and human annotation results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original reward-model experiments, labeling-strategy simulations, and human survey outcomes, including Appendix J.

M1.justification: The DataInf-based influence estimation, OPORP gradient compression, reward model, and SVM-based labeling-strategy update remain identical.

E1.justification: Both use the same Anthropic-HH and HelpSteer2 data for length and sycophancy bias detection, labeling-strategy oversight, and appendix evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Pro, confidence, entropy, Mahalanobis and KNN for bias detection; Mahalanobis and KNN for strategy oversight; and DataInf for efficiency and estimation comparisons.

E3.justification: Data splits, corruption rates, sample sizes, four-epoch Llama-3-8B training, evaluation metrics, and appendix experimental procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same validation-set composition, size and distribution ablations, few-shot comparisons, retraining analyses, qualitative examples, and original-data human surveys.

E5.justification: Both retain Figure 12's five-trial averages and error bars and Figure 14's averages over 20 random subsets. No statistical reporting is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 9 retains influence AUCs of 0.800 and 0.711, while Table 12 retains mislabeled counts of 47 versus 13 and 55 versus 33.

T1.justification: The influence-function definitions, assumptions and derivations in Sections 3–4, together with the appendix mathematics, are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both retain the same claims about efficient influence estimation, detecting labeler biases, and guiding labeling strategies toward expert preferences, including the claimed 2.5-fold speedup.

C2.justification: Interpretations of validation-set dependence, distribution shift and bias mitigation are identical. Limitations concerning approximation error, restricted bias coverage and simulated labeling strategies are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, compression, prompt and data-construction details are unchanged, as is source-code access information. The changed arXiv self-link only identifies the newer version.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the references retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the relationships to DataInf and scalable oversight.

P1.justification: The acknowledgments replace NRF grant RS-2023-00256259 with RS-2024-00414822. The arXiv stamp changes from v2, 4 June 2025, to v3, 1 September 2025; other wording and document structure match.

P2.justification: Figures 1–16, Tables 1–12, Algorithm 1, captions and page layout are unchanged. The administrative text substitutions cause no reorganization or display changes.

improvement.justification: Only the version stamp and funding identifier change. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information and organization remain identical, establishing no meaningful net difference in paper quality.
